findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Quantify 'ordinary run variation' in AC7 (e.g. derive a numeric variance band from the recent post-DNS green runs and require the observed macOS decrease to exceed it) so the retention oracle is deterministic.
evidence: 'a macOS runner-time decrease beyond recent run variation with no Ubuntu regression'
'macOS runner time decreases beyond ordinary run variation'
No numeric variance band or threshold is stated for 'ordinary run variation'
findings.finding: The retention oracle in AC7 hinges on a macOS runner-time decrease 'beyond recent run variation' / 'beyond ordinary run variation', but the plan never quantifies that variation (no baseline variance, standard deviation, or numeric threshold). The retain/reject decision is therefore subjective.
scenarios: Implementation run shows a 1-2s macOS decrease; reviewer cannot tell if this exceeds noise without a stated variance band
Two evaluators reach opposite retain/reject conclusions from the same numbers
findings.suggested_fix: State the variance band explicitly, e.g. 'compute mean and stddev of macOS default/integration wall time across the last N post-DNS green runs; retain only if the RAM-disk run's macOS time is below (mean - k*stddev)'.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State how the control comparison isolates the RAM-disk effect from per-change workload differences (e.g. anchor to identical collection/pass/skip counts already asserted, and compare against the aggregate of recent green runs on the same selectors rather than a single unrelated run) so the observed decrease is attributable to storage placement.
evidence: 'Use the next full Verify run initiated by another session as the timing control.'
'Compare its macOS default/integration/job wall times with the unrelated control and recent post-DNS green runs'
An unrelated change runs a different diff but the same selectors; wall-time deltas conflate change content with storage placement
findings.finding: The timing control is an 'unrelated full Gerrit Verify run' for a different change, whose test workload differs from the RAM-disk change's run. Comparing wall times across two different changes conflates the RAM-disk effect with per-change content/workload differences, so the comparison may not actually prove the RAM disk caused any observed macOS decrease.
findings.location: Plan steps 1 and 6; AC1 and AC7
scenarios: The unrelated control happens to run on a less-loaded runner, masking or faking the RAM-disk savings
Reviewer credits a decrease to the RAM disk that is actually from a lighter unrelated change

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm and state in the plan that the APFS RAM-disk mount path is outside the macOS tmp-cleaner's reap scope (i.e. not under /tmp or a periodically-cleaned directory), so relocating basetemps off runner.temp does not reintroduce the mid-run FileNotFoundError cascade the runner.temp choice was made to avoid.
evidence: _build-and-test.yml lines 608-611: 'Pin --basetemp under the runner temp (not /tmp): on long (10-16 min) runs the macOS tmp-cleaner reaps pytest's default /tmp/pytest-of-* basetemp mid-run, producing a spurious FileNotFoundError cascade'
Plan Context: 'The workflow deliberately uses runner.temp rather than /tmp because the macOS tmp cleaner previously deleted live test trees.'
Plan step 3 routes both selectors to 'separate basetemps below that mount' but does not address tmp-cleaner scope for the new mount point.
findings.finding: The plan relocates pytest basetemps from runner.temp onto a newly-created APFS RAM-disk mount but never confirms that this mount is outside the macOS tmp-cleaner's reap scope. The workflow chose runner.temp precisely because the macOS tmp-cleaner previously deleted live /tmp/pytest-of-* trees mid-run, causing a spurious FileNotFoundError cascade; moving off runner.temp without asserting the new mount's immunity risks reintroducing that exact failure.
findings.location: Plan step 3 and Context ('The workflow deliberately uses runner.temp rather than /tmp because the macOS tmp cleaner previously deleted live test trees')
scenarios: A macOS default+integration run exceeding 10-16 minutes where the tmp-cleaner scans the RAM-disk mount path and reaps a live basetemp, recreating the FileNotFoundError cascade the runner.temp choice was designed to prevent.

No mention of an inline workflow comment, ADR, or AGENTS.md note explaining the RAM-disk rationale and the runner.temp tmp-cleaner history that motivated it
findings.finding: The plan introduces a novel, platform-specific CI mechanism (an ephemeral APFS RAM disk in the shared build/test workflow) but does not specify where the rationale/lifecycle is documented for future maintainers beyond the contract tests. A future editor of _build-and-test.yml could remove or break the macOS-only guard without understanding why it exists.
scenarios: A later contributor simplifies the workflow and drops the macOS RAM-disk branch, silently reverting the speedup or reintroducing the tmp-cleaner bug

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Name and verify (against `hdiutil`/`diskutil` --help/man) the exact create/mount/detach command surface for the RAM disk — including the ram:// sector-count unit and whether the volume is APFS or HFS+ — so step 3/4 and AC3/AC5 assert a command sequence that actually exists rather than an unconfirmed 'APFS RAM disk'.
evidence: Plan step 3: 'create an APFS RAM disk only when runner.os is macOS ... Publish its mount path through a step output'
Plan step 4: 'detach the exact device created by setup after both pytest tiers'
Contract card production_path: 'GitHub Actions creates an ephemeral APFS RAM device ... then cleanup detaches only that device'
Read of .github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml: the test job writes --basetemp under runner.temp and has NO hdiutil/diskutil step today, so this is a new CLI integration for the repo

The two cited precedents are named but the plan does not transcribe their command lines; APFS-specific RAM-disk creation (synthesized container on a ram device) differs materially from the HFS+ `diskutil erasevolume HFS+ ram $(hdiutil attach -nomount ram://N)` idiom

EVIDENCE CLASS: Partially-verified — the RAM-disk-on-macOS mechanism exists and has OSS precedent, but the specific create/mount/detach command surface and the APFS filesystem choice are unconfirmed in the plan text
findings.finding: The plan asserts creating/detaching a macOS 'APFS RAM disk' but never names the specific CLI subcommands and flags it depends on (hdiutil attach -nomount ram://<sectors>, diskutil apfs create / erasevolume, hdiutil detach / diskutil eject) — the command surface is UNVERIFIED against --help/man, and the APFS-vs-HFS+ choice (Apple precedent is APFS; the common erasevolume idiom yields HFS+) is asserted without confirmation.
findings.location: Plan step 3 ("create an APFS RAM disk"); step 4 ("detach the exact device created by setup"); contract card production_path; AC line 3 / AC line 5
scenarios: Implementation step 3 picks `diskutil erasevolume HFS+` (producing HFS+, not the asserted APFS) and the AC3/AC5 'APFS' assertions become inaccurate
hdiutil ram:// sector arithmetic (bytes vs 512-byte sectors) is miscomputed from the step-2 sizing, creating a device of the wrong size
Detach uses a subcommand/flag that leaves the synthesized APFS container attached, so the always() cleanup fails to remove 'only the exact device'
findings.suggested_fix: In step 3, transcribe the concrete commands (e.g., DEV=$(hdiutil attach -nomount ram://$SECTORS); diskutil erasevolume APFS RebarBasetemp "$DEV") with SECTORS derived from step-2 bytes / 512, and in step 4 the matching detach (hdiutil detach "$DEV"), verifying each verb/flag against the tool's man page; reconcile the APFS-vs-HFS+ wording with whatever the verified command produces.
